# Supplementary geometric and deterministic details {#sec-appendix-geometry}

## The Stiefel tangent and invariance statements

The tangent space at $W\in\mathrm{St}(d,r)$ is

$$
T_W\mathrm{St}(d,r)
=\{U\in\mathbb R^{d\times r}:W^\top U+U^\top W=0\}.
$$

For $G(\mu,W,x)$ from @eq-oja-observable, $W^\top G=0$.  Hence $G$ is not merely tangent: it is horizontal, with the particularly simple polar retraction @eq-polar-retraction.  Its image satisfies

$$
R_W(U)^\top R_W(U)
=(I+U^\top U)^{-1/2}(I+U^\top U)
 (I+U^\top U)^{-1/2}=I_r.
$$

The averaged field has the same horizontal form, so any ODE solution starting from a Stiefel matrix remains on Stiefel.  Indeed

$$
\frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt}(W^\top W)
=W^\top\dot W+\dot W^\top W=0.
$$

This is why the limiting problem does not require extending the ODE away from the manifold to *define its actual solution*, even though ambient Euclidean coordinates are used for stochastic error estimates.

## Positive definiteness of the covariance iterate

The first two recursions are exactly Euclidean.  The covariance recursion is

$$
\Gamma_{n+1}=(1-\gamma_{n+1})\Gamma_n+
\gamma_{n+1}(X_{n+1}-\mu_n)(X_{n+1}-\mu_n)^\top.
$$

As $0<\gamma_{n+1}<1$ and the second term is positive semidefinite,

$$
\Gamma_{n+1}\succeq(1-\gamma_{n+1})\Gamma_n\succ0.
$$

Thus $\Gamma_n$ stays positive definite at every **finite** iteration.  This does not establish that its smallest eigenvalue stays bounded away from zero as $n\to\infty$.  Such a uniform lower bound requires the eventual-compactness/stability argument; the distinction is central to @eq-compact-eigenvalue-bounds.

## The reconstruction-error objective and its geometric interpretation

The residual projector $P_W=I-WW^\top$ is symmetric and idempotent.  Therefore the expected reconstruction error in @eq-reconstruction-energy is equivalently

$
\mathcal R(\mu,W)
=\frac12\big(\operatorname{tr}Q(\mu)
-\operatorname{tr}(W^\top Q(\mu)W)\big).
$

At fixed $\mu$, minimizing $\mathcal R$ means maximizing the variance explained by $W$.  On the Stiefel manifold its negative Riemannian gradient is exactly the averaged sample-driven Oja field; see @lem-reconstruction-gradient.  The moving centring parameter contributes the further nonpositive term $-\|P_W(\mu-m)\|^2$ to the derivative.  Thus the composite functional @eq-composite-energy is a direct sum of the mean--covariance energy and an objective actually decreased by the complete averaged recursion.

## Invariant subspaces and finitely many energy values

Let $C=U\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_d)U^\top$, counting eigenvalues with multiplicity.  If $\operatorname{span}(W)$ is invariant under the symmetric $C$, it is a direct sum of subspaces of eigenspaces.  The trace $\operatorname{tr}(W^\top CW)$ equals a sum of exactly $r$ entries from this eigenvalue list.  The number of possible sums is finite, although there can be infinitely many orthonormal bases representing the same invariant subspace, and even infinitely many invariant subspaces when eigenvalues repeat.  Therefore $\widetilde w_L(\mathcal E)$ is a finite subset of $\mathbb R$, as required by @benaim1999, Proposition 6.4.
